newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister to meet PM amid scandal talk.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister to meet PM amid scandal talk.

text.p: An official said on Saturday that Russia's justice minister would meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin shortly amid media controversy over a secretly-shot video film alleged to show the minister in a sauna.
"It is a fact that certain circumstances require an explanation from the minister," the head of the government's culture and information department, Igor Shabdurasulov, told Ekho Moskvy radio.
"I believe the explanation will be given before the prime minister leaves on a trip (on Sunday to New York)," he added.

Shabdurasulov's comments came after the monthly Top Secret newspaper published grainy photographs taken from the video, which it alleged showed Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyov in a night club sauna with women.

"For the time being, not all the details concerning the appearance of this publication are known, but if the facts (given in the article) are confirmed then any state official...would be obliged, in the best scenario, to resign," Shabdurasulov said.
In a country long known for official secrecy, few, if any, government ministers have been forced to resign due to scandals.
A Justice Ministry spokesman told Reuters that Kovalyov, 53, would react in due course to the allegations against him.
"The minister is an extremely decent person, and being a highly qualified lawyer he is well able to defend himself (against such allegations)," said spokesman Viktor Osokin.

Kovalyov, a former law professor and a member of Russia's Security Council, became Justice Minister in January 1995. The Top Secret paper, which is sensationalist but well-connected, said the video dated back to September 1995.
